title: Getting Claude Code to model motorcycle lean: knee-down sparks past 47°, plus lowside and highside crashes
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
Kneespark is a Grand Prix bike racer for the browser. The hard part with bikes is that cornering isn’t steering. Lean angle, braking and throttle all have to balance, or you crash. I made it with Claude Code to see how well it handles that.

**Who made what:**

* **Code:** all written with Claude Code
* **Assets:** bike and helmet models from Sketchfab (CC BY 4.0, repainted), rider animations from Mixamo, textures and skies from Poly Haven (CC0), and sounds from Freesound (CC0)

**Workflow that worked:**

1. **Lean first, on a flat loop.** Lean grows with speed, and past about 47° the knee slider hits the tarmac and throws sparks. Getting lean to feel right before anything else made everything after easier.
2. **Crash rules as clear conditions.** Too much brake at full lean is a lowside, and too much throttle is a highside. Describing each crash as “this input at this lean” got cleaner results than “make crashes realistic”.
3. **Weight transfer after that.** Wheelies on hard exits, and the rear lifting under heavy braking.
4. **Assists as toggles.** Traction control, anti-wheelie, ABS and a lean-angle assist are all on by default. Building them as separate layers you can switch off made it easy to test the raw physics underneath.
5. **Hilly tracks last.** Three circuits with climbs, drops and crests, which change grip and braking points. Plus 19 rivals who slipstream and outbrake you.

Riders who crash get caught by air fences and are back on the bike in a few seconds, so races keep moving. There are four camera views: chase, helmet, onboard and trackside TV.

[https://vinish.dev/kneespark-motorcycle-racing-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/kneespark-motorcycle-racing-browser-based-game)

Anyone else done two-wheeled physics with AI? Curious how you handled lean and crashes.
